answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated results or collusion. Audits should sample jobs unpredictably and compare outputs against verifiable evidence, so creating many identities does not let an attacker predict which will be checked. A saffron seller and a relic hunter may both wander the market, but each new Sybil must tie up real capital and risk losing it; identities are cheap, repeated accountable participation is not.
